Predict from a rdistnn_plqr_result object at new targets (experimental)

Source: R/user-dnn-plqr-methods.R
predict.rdistnn_plqr_result.Rd

Predict from a rdistnn_plqr_result object at new targets (experimental)

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_plqr_result'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  se.fit = FALSE,
  interval = c("none", "confidence"),
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A rdistnn_plqr_result object from plqr_dnn().

newdata

Optional matrix/data frame of target covariates.

X0

Optional numeric matrix of targets (rows).

x0

Optional numeric vector for a single target.

se.fit

Logical; if TRUE, also return direct coefficient standard errors. The fitted object must retain density values from density or density_col.

interval

One of "none" or "confidence".

level

Confidence level for interval output.

...

Not used.

Value

With interval = "none" and se.fit = FALSE, a coefficient matrix with one row per PLQR coefficient and one column per target. With se.fit = TRUE, a list with fit and se.fit matrices. With interval = "confidence", a list with fit, lwr, and upr matrices, and also se.fit when requested. The coefficient source is attached to the fit as attr(., "theta_source").

Details

The returned fit matrix repeats the supplied theta_eval (meta$theta_source = "supplied"). Target-specific variation enters only through the DNN weights and the resulting direct-sandwich standard errors; no target-specific PLQR root is solved.

Coefficient uncertainty requires a fit with density or density_col. moment_se describes score variation and is not a coefficient standard error. Prediction standard errors always use the analytic sandwich meat, regardless of the fit's theta_meat choice, because the fitted object does not retain the outcome data needed to re-run the jackknife at new targets.

Lifecycle

Experimental. The PLQR API and inference interfaces may change.

See also

plqr_dnn().

Examples

set.seed(3)
demo <- plqr_demo_data(n = 80, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 3)
fit <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  theta_eval = demo$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L, s = 5L,
  se = FALSE
)
predict(fit, x0 = c(0.2, -0.1))
#>    target_1
#> D1      0.5
#> D2      0.5
#> attr(,"theta_source")
#> [1] "supplied"
